RAG vs Agentic RAG vs Graph RAG

Three ways to give a model your own data before it answers. Classic RAG finds similar text once; agentic RAG lets agents plan and check the search; graph RAG searches through connections between things. Run one question through each, flip the switches, and tap any block.

Swipe sideways to see all three.
Press a ▶ button to follow one question, or tap a block.
RAGAgentic RAGGraph RAG
RetrievesSimilar text chunks, onceFrom several sources, as often as the evaluator asksEntities and their links (local) or community summaries (global)
Model calls13 or more (plan, evaluate, answer)1 (local); one per batch of reports plus a final call (global)
Built ahead of timeChunks + vector indexSame, plus tool and API accessKnowledge graph, communities and their reports: the costly part
Good atLook-ups in your documentsMulti-part questions, checking its own retrievalRelationships; themes across a whole collection
Weak atWrong chunks go unnoticedLatency, cost, harder to testKeeping the graph current; cost of global search

Call counts follow the flows drawn above; real systems vary (our reading).

Which one should you start with?

Pick the kind of question your users ask most.

Rule of thumb (our reading): start with classic RAG and a good reranker; add agents when questions need several searches or a check; build a graph when the questions are about relationships or the whole collection. Graph RAG with local and global search follows the approach Microsoft Research published as GraphRAG.
